_note: Street Runner's delivery sources in Paris (src/game/delivery.ts `sources`). Every name is INVENTED, on purpose: no real business is named or implied. Invented kitchens at plausible places (owner, 2026-10-30: 'regionally appropriate (baguettes, croissants, camembert, quiche, escargot, bouillabaise, but then also with a smattering of curry and bagels and such)'). Mostly French, with the rest where Paris keeps it: curry in the Passage Brady and at La Chapelle, bagels and falafel in the Rue des Rosiers, ramen in the Rue Sainte-Anne, pho on the Avenue de Choisy, couscous at the Goutte d'Or, dumplings in Belleville, crêpes by Montparnasse.

restaurants.name: Le Moulin à Selle
restaurants.blurb: Up the Rue Lepic, where the only thing rising faster than the dough is your heart rate.

items.name: baguette tradition
items.blurb: Still warm. Carry it under your arm, as the law more or less requires.

items.name: pain au chocolat
items.blurb: Do not call it a chocolatine this far north.

items.name: pain de campagne
items.blurb: Weighs about the same as a touring pannier.

restaurants.name: Boulangerie du Grand Plateau
restaurants.blurb: Flat ride, flaky crust, and a queue out of the door by seven.

items.name: dozen croissants
items.blurb: Two hundred layers of butter and no crash protection.

items.name: baguette
items.blurb: The end is already missing. The baker swears it wasn't him.

items.name: chausson aux pommes
items.blurb: Apple turnover, molten inside, smug outside.

restaurants.name: L'Escargot à Pignon
restaurants.blurb: Fixed-gear snails. They have never once been late, because nobody expects them.

items.name: dozen escargots
items.blurb: In garlic butter, in their shells, on a dimpled dish. Corner gently.

items.name: cuisses de grenouille
items.blurb: Frogs' legs: the only legs in this city fresher than yours.

items.name: soupe à l'oignon
items.blurb: A lid of molten Gruyère holding back a lake.

restaurants.name: Fromagerie de la Roue Libre
restaurants.blurb: Coast down the Rue Cler and let your nose do the navigating.

items.name: camembert de Normandie
items.blurb: Runny by the Pont de l'Alma. Riders behind you will know.

items.name: wedge of comté
items.blurb: Aged twenty-four months, which is longer than your last chain.

items.name: plateau de fromages
items.blurb: Seven cheeses arranged by someone who will check.

restaurants.name: Au Camembert Sans Frein
restaurants.blurb: Brakeless cheese, on the market street at Lévis. It stops when it wants to.

items.name: baked camembert
items.blurb: Liquid in the box. Keep it level, whatever the cobbles say.

items.name: baguette and brie
items.blurb: Lunch, according to every Parisian's doctor but their own.

restaurants.name: Au Petit Dérailleur
restaurants.blurb: On the Rue des Martyrs, which is named for what the climb does to you.

items.name: quiche lorraine
items.blurb: Bacon, cream, and absolutely no cheese, or Lorraine will hear about it.

items.name: quiche aux poireaux
items.blurb: Leek quiche, for the rider who has made peace with leeks.

items.name: salade de chèvre chaud
items.blurb: Warm goat's cheese on toast, on lettuce, on borrowed time.

restaurants.name: Le Chat Qui Pédale
restaurants.blurb: Down the Mouffetard, and mind the cobbles with that dish.

items.name: quiche du jour
items.blurb: What day is it? The quiche knows.

items.name: ratatouille
items.blurb: Yes, like the film. No, the chef is not a rat. Probably.

items.name: gratin dauphinois
items.blurb: Potatoes and cream, a recovery drink in solid form.

restaurants.name: La Bouillabaisse du Vieux-Port
restaurants.blurb: Eight hundred kilometres from Marseille and still arguing about the recipe.

items.name: bouillabaisse
items.blurb: Saffron, rockfish and a very full pot. Every pothole is a tragedy.

items.name: moules marinière
items.blurb: A kilo of mussels, rattling like a loose mudguard.

items.name: sole meunière
items.blurb: Browned butter, one lemon, no second chances.

restaurants.name: L'Éternel Second
restaurants.blurb: Never once first to your door, and proud of the podiums.

items.name: confit de canard
items.blurb: Duck, slow in its own fat. The opposite of your delivery.

items.name: steak frites
items.blurb: Saignant. The frites have about four minutes to live.

items.name: tarte tatin
items.blurb: Upside down on purpose, unlike you on the Boulevard.

restaurants.name: Le Peloton Gourmand
restaurants.blurb: A great mirrored room on the Boulevard du Montparnasse, and everybody drafting the waiter.

items.name: choucroute garnie
items.blurb: Sauerkraut and five kinds of pig, all in the breakaway.

items.name: plateau de fruits de mer
items.blurb: Oysters on crushed ice, in a box, on a bike, in the sun.

restaurants.name: Crêperie du Tourmalet
restaurants.blurb: On the crêperie street behind the Breton trains' old station, flat as the batter.

items.name: galette complète
items.blurb: Buckwheat, ham, cheese, an egg, and a cider you may not carry.

items.name: crêpe Suzette
items.blurb: Flambéed to order. The flames are out. Mostly.

items.name: kouign-amann
items.blurb: Breton for 'butter cake', and for 'that was the climb sorted'.

restaurants.name: La Lanterne Rouge
restaurants.blurb: Dead last into every stage and the kitchen has never apologised.

items.name: bœuf bourguignon
items.blurb: Six hours in the pot. Six minutes on your bike. Don't waste it.

items.name: coq au vin
items.blurb: A whole bottle went into this bird. Ride straight.

restaurants.name: Pâtisserie du Maillot Jaune
restaurants.blurb: The Rue du Bac's lightest climbers, in a box with a ribbon.

items.name: box of macarons
items.blurb: Twelve colours, each one crushed by a stern look.

items.name: éclair au café
items.blurb: Glazed, slender, and aerodynamically your best effort today.

items.name: mille-feuille
items.blurb: A thousand leaves, and each of them is going to end up on your jersey.

restaurants.name: Tartine & Guidon
restaurants.blurb: By the Marché des Enfants-Rouges, with handlebars over the bar.

items.name: croque-monsieur
items.blurb: Ham, béchamel, a good crust. The croque-madame is the same with an egg, and a warning.

items.name: jambon-beurre
items.blurb: Half a baguette, ham, butter, and nothing else, ever.

restaurants.name: Le Bidon du Canal
restaurants.blurb: Picnics for the Canal Saint-Martin, its iron bridges and its long afternoons.

items.name: picnic hamper
items.blurb: Bread, saucisson, cheese. The corkscrew is your problem.

items.name: pot de rillettes
items.blurb: Pork, shredded and potted. Holds up better than you will.

restaurants.name: Le Petit Braquet
restaurants.blurb: Low gear, low lights, Rue de Charonne.

items.name: blanquette de veau
items.blurb: A white stew in a white box. You are wearing black. Good.

items.name: moules-frites
items.blurb: Belgian, they say. Do not say so at this door.

restaurants.name: Le Pied de Pédale
restaurants.blurb: Open all night by the old Halles, for market porters who no longer exist.

items.name: onion soup gratinée
items.blurb: Three in the morning in a bowl.

items.name: pied de cochon
items.blurb: Pig's trotter, breadcrumbed, grilled, and a fine joke about your cadence.

restaurants.name: Le Sprint de l'Étoile
restaurants.blurb: White tablecloths off the Avenue Victor-Hugo, for the people who really did finish on the Champs.

items.name: foie gras
items.blurb: On a tiny toast, in a large box, with a card.

items.name: gratin de homard
items.blurb: Half a lobster, whose ride ends better than yours.

restaurants.name: La Guinguette du Lac
restaurants.blurb: Sandwiches for the Bois, and an accordion you can't escape.

items.name: sandwich au saucisson
items.blurb: Dry sausage, salted butter, and a very long way to the car.

items.name: tarte aux pommes
items.blurb: Whole, in its tin. Do not race the joggers.

restaurants.name: La Flamme Rouge
restaurants.blurb: One kilometre to go, and nobody here has ever hurried it. The Batignolles' neighbourhood table.

items.name: tarte flambée
items.blurb: Alsace's thin one: crème fraîche, onions, lardons, and don't call it pizza.

items.name: cassoulet
items.blurb: Beans, duck, sausage. Your climbing is over for today.

restaurants.name: Le Tonneau de Bercy
restaurants.blurb: In the old wine warehouses, where the rails still run through the cobbles.

items.name: planche de charcuterie
items.blurb: Saucisson, terrine, cornichons: all the food groups.

items.name: œufs mayonnaise
items.blurb: The classic. Soft eggs, stiff mayo, hard cobbles.

restaurants.name: Curry du Passage
restaurants.blurb: Under the Passage Brady's cracked glass, where it has smelled wonderful since the seventies.

items.name: butter chicken
items.blurb: Paris's favourite curry, and it stains like a chain.

items.name: lamb vindaloo
items.blurb: You'll be the fastest thing on the Boulevard de Strasbourg.

items.name: garlic naan
items.blurb: Folded in foil. Rolls nicely in a bottle cage.

restaurants.name: Petite Jaffna
restaurants.blurb: Up at La Chapelle, the Faubourg's Little Sri Lanka.

items.name: masala dosa
items.blurb: A crisp crêpe as long as your top tube. Paris understands.

items.name: chicken kottu roti
items.blurb: Chopped on the griddle, loud enough to hear from the Métro.

restaurants.name: L'Anneau Magique
restaurants.blurb: Rue des Rosiers: hand-boiled rings, two doors from an argument about the best falafel.

items.name: bagel with salmon
items.blurb: Lox and cream cheese. Hole included at no extra charge.

items.name: bagel pastrami
items.blurb: New York's, by way of the Marais, and vice versa.

items.name: babka
items.blurb: Chocolate, twisted. Like your frame after that kerb.

restaurants.name: Falafel au Guidon
restaurants.blurb: Eaten standing up in the Rue des Rosiers, or in your case, moving.

items.name: falafel pita
items.blurb: Stuffed past what any pita should bear. Mind the tahini.

items.name: shawarma plate
items.blurb: Off the spit, and off your route if you take the wrong cobbles.

restaurants.name: Tonkotsu Tandem
restaurants.blurb: On the Rue Sainte-Anne, where the queue for ramen is its own arrondissement.

items.name: tonkotsu ramen
items.blurb: Twelve-hour broth. Two-minute noodles, on the clock.

items.name: gyoza
items.blurb: Six pan-fried dumplings, crisp side up.

restaurants.name: Phở de la Porte de Choisy
restaurants.blurb: Deep in the 13th's towers, the real Chinatown of Paris.

items.name: phở bò
items.blurb: A quart of hot broth in a bag. It's fine. It's fine.

items.name: bánh mì
items.blurb: A baguette that has seen the world and come home better.

restaurants.name: Le Dragon de Belleville
restaurants.blurb: Dumplings at the top of a long, steep street. You have been warned.

items.name: steamed dumplings
items.blurb: Wenzhou-style, by the dozen, straight up the hill.

items.name: duck with rice
items.blurb: Lacquered and hanging in the window until you came along.

restaurants.name: Le Couscous de la Goutte d'Or
restaurants.blurb: Behind Barbès, on Friday, with everybody's uncle.

items.name: couscous royal
items.blurb: Lamb, merguez, chicken, and enough semolina to re-ballast the Ligne 2.

items.name: tagine aux pruneaux
items.blurb: Lamb and prunes, in a pot with a very pointy hat.

items.name: mint tea
items.blurb: Sweet, scalding, and poured from a height you can't match.
